the political use of symbols is important in the process of peace building and conflict transformation.

the political use of symbols and symbolism and their significance for the establishment of new political orders in post‐conflict situations.

symbols are not as important as they are often claimed to be.

symbols of unity and concord are difficult to achieve in post‐settle societies, particularly when the political and social divisions are so entrenched.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
symbols and symbolism are central to political processes and political transitions.
symbols and symbolism are important political resources and that their usage in the political sphere is likely to increase in the future.
the use of symbols and symbolism has been an important feature of the political process in deeply divided societies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the symbolic attempts at unity and accord are not always successful and that the symbols of discord often continue to have more salience than the symbols of unity and harmony.
the political use of symbols is a complex process, and that the use of symbols of unity and concord in post‐settle periods is often fraught with difficulties.
